diagnostic_fixture.full_input: Fastlegen er riktig inngang. Ungdomssenteret kan hjelpe.

service_nouns_as_engine_computed.inventory_status: NEVER_EVALUATED - engine guard 'unknown = [] if route else _unknown_service_nouns(...)' skips noun scan when any inventory term present

service_nouns_ground_truth.inventory_status: OUT_OF_INVENTORY - stem 'senter' not covered by any ROUTE_TERMS hit

BC_ROUTE_UNKNOWN_SERVICE_01.why: guard evaluates unknown nouns only when no inventory route term exists anywhere in output; inventory term 'fastlege' in clause 0 suppressed the scan for 'ungdomssenteret' in clause 1

BC_ROUTE_ASSERTED_01.why: assertion marker 'riktig inngang' present at output level; no clause-locality check relates operator to a specific route proposition

BC_ROUTE_VAGUE_01.why: vague markers require 'not route'; inventory term present so vague path disabled even though clause 1 contains 'hjelpe'

why_deterministic_instead_of_abstain: 1. Whole-output rule evaluation: all marker sets are computed over the full text; no clause/proposition scoping exists in the engine.
2. Operator-noun decoupling: BC_ROUTE_ASSERTED_01 fires on any assertion marker anywhere, licensing a deterministic label for the whole output regardless of which clause's route noun it grounds.
3. Suppressed unknown-noun guard: the out-of-inventory guard (V1.6A.1 fix) is bypassed whenever an unrelated inventory term appears in another clause, so 'ungdomssenteret' is never tested.

4. No competition check: two route propositions in one output are never compared for whether both can be grounded; clause 1 (inventory noun + assertion) silently absorbs clause 2 (unknown noun + vague capability wording).
generalized_failure_condition: A deterministic route label may be emitted when an operator in one clause licenses a route proposition while a different clause contains a service noun that cannot be grounded by any high-precision rule. The engine cannot see clause boundaries, so the ungrounded proposition is invisible.
